data.name: Darbee
data.long_meaning: In Greek, Darbee derives from the word 'dear,' meaning 'beloved' or 'precious.' This name was used in ancient Greece for both boys and girls. In Christian tradition, it is associated with the beloved disciple John, who was called the 'beloved disciple' in the New Testament.

In a Christian context, it may refer to the head or leader of the Church, such as Jesus Christ (Matthew 16:16).

in_greek.name: Δαρβή
in_greek.long_meaning: Δαρβή (Darbē) - ἀρχηγός (archegos) - leader, chief, or head. In the New Testament, Jesus Christ is referred to as the Head of the Church (Colossians 1:18). Δαρβή (Darbē) may also be related to the Greek word ἀρχή (archē) - beginning, origin, or principle, as in the beginning of creation (Genesis 1:1).
